description.narrative: Project Outcomes: Amid growing grid instability driven by the rapid expansion of renewables, IFC aims to enhance electricity reliability in Romania while simultaneously reducing the countrys GHG emissions. The Project supports EU-wide NDC objectives of a 55% emissions reduction by 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, as well as Romanias national plan to phase out coal by 2032. It would demonstrate large-scale standalone BESS in a market where deployment remains limited despite government targets of 1.2 GW by 2030 and available subsidy support. The Project will also showcase the commercial viability of utility-scale BESS in Romania and help catalyze further private-sector investment, economic activity, and employment.

The proposed investment comprises a Romanian greenfield portfolio of five standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) being developed by Aukera BV, designed to provide two-hour storage and grid-balancing services across four key nodes in the countrys North-East and South-East (Project). The Project will have a total capacity of up to 0.95 GW / 1.9 GWh and will be financed in two stages: - Stage I: Short-term construction bridge financing for two BESS assets in the same location totalling 250 MW; and - Stage II: Long-term financing of three BESS assets in three different locations totalling up to 700 MW, along with the refinancing of Stage I assets. By adding flexible capacity where renewable penetration and price volatility are rising, the Project supports Romanias grid reliability, energy security, and decarbonization trajectory, whilst reducing price volatility.
